# FlareButton

`Flare.Components.FlareButton`

## Parameters

| `AriaLabel` | `string?` | `` | Parameter |  | Accessible label for the button, forwarded as aria-label. |
| `AriaPressed` | `bool?` | `` | Parameter |  | Toggle state, forwarded as aria-pressed. Left null the attribute is absent and the button is an ordinary command; false renders aria-pressed="false", which is what makes assistive technology announce a toggle that is currently off rather than a plain button. The distinction is why this is nullable: an absent attribute and an explicit "false" are different controls, not the same control in different states. |
| `ChildContent` | `RenderFragment?` | `` | Parameter |  | Button label and inner content. |
| `Color` | `FlareColor` | `` | Parameter |  | Color of the button. Use a semantic preset (FlareColor.Primary) - rendered via a shared CSS class (fast path) - or an arbitrary color via FlareColor.Custom("#FF0000") / @("#FF0000"), which inlines the local color tokens (filled text auto-contrasted, or set via OnColor). Default keeps the theme default. |
